rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods - three-season field trial at Tel Amara station (1997-1999) with drip/fertigation vs macro-sprinkler treatments, randomized block design, 15N microplots, tensiometers, neutron probe and tensionics soil-solution extractors at 30/60/80 cm. Q2: Section 'Nitrate leaching evaluation' and Figure 6 - significantly higher nitrate concentrations below the roots (60 and 80 cm) under sprinkler, while fertigation and drip treatments showed steady very low nitrate at 80 cm and nitrate restricted to the root zone (40 cm); estimated N leached below root zone under 3 kg/ha for drip vs about 55 kg/ha for sprinkler; Abstract and Conclusions repeat that N stayed in the root zone under drip. Q4: 'Fertilizer use efficiency' section - sprinkler described as one-dimensional flow wetting the full bed width; tensiometers showed soil head potential in the upper layer of -175 to -100 mbar under sprinkler and weak fluctuation at 60 cm (-100 to -50 mbar) indicating deeper water penetration; neutron probe showed roots removed relatively more water (39%) from the 30-60 cm layer under sprinkler; irrigation-efficiency calculation estimated 322 mm water lost to subsoil under sprinkler vs 40-50 mm under drip.
rows.notes: Leaching result rests essentially on one method (tensionic soil-solution nitrate at three depths); the leached-N estimate combines the same concentrations with literature-derived irrigation efficiencies, so not counted as independent triangulation. Single site, soil (clay Typic Xerorthent) and crop (potato cv Spunta); 1999 'large-scale' trial used 1250 m2 plots, still plot scale. Sprinkler treatment was in a nearby non-randomized area; this is not stated by the authors as a limitation. No dispersion measure is reported for the nitrate concentrations in Figure 6 (only 'significantly higher'); standard errors appear only for shoot dry matter (Figure 3). No condition for the drip effect is stated as a requirement beyond generic recommendations on cost efficiency.

notes: Full text appears complete. Study compares drip/fertigation with macro-sprinkler for N recovery and nitrate movement in one Lebanese clay soil over three spring potato seasons.
